_comment: Copy this file to live.config.json in this folder (git ignores that name), fill in a TEST account, start the game servers, then run: npm run test:live

Two limits of the servers can lock you out if you run this too often. (1) The certifier blocks the test account from an address for 15 seconds after one wrong password, and for 15 minutes after three in a row; a good login clears the count. A run sends one wrong password from this PC and one from the simulated address 10.0.0.1, so wait 15 seconds between runs. (2) Until the certifier and the login server are rebuilt with flood-limiter-gateway.patch and have a Gateway "127.0.0.1" line (server-patches/README.md), their accept limiter counts connections from one address that arrive less than 200 ms apart; after 50 of them it cuts every connection from that address for about 10 minutes, and the count never decays. The test keeps its connections 300 ms apart and ends each flow before the next, but do not loop it.

gateway: the test runs this gateway inside its own process. listen.port must be free (8091 does not clash with a gateway on 8090). trustedProxies must list 127.0.0.1, because the test simulates other addresses with X-Forwarded-For.

certifierPatched: set true only when the rebuilt Certifier.exe (server-patches/README.md) is running and Certifier.ini has a Gateway "127.0.0.1" line. It turns on the test that a wrong password from one address does not block another.

bannedTestAddress: an address you added to Program/IPCut.ini (restart the account server afterwards), for example "10.0.0.99", or null. It turns on the banned-address test, which also needs certifierPatched.
account, password, bankPin: a throwaway account with at least one empty character slot. The test creates WebTest and 3 digits in the first empty slot with this Bank PIN, then deletes it.

world: the world test (npm run test:live:world) is skipped without this section. accounts: two throwaway accounts with their Bank PINs; the first walks, the second watches. Each uses its first character, which must stand in Flaris within sight of the other's (a new character does); an account without a character gets WebWalk and 3 digits, made first and deleted at the end with its Bank PIN. It also needs gateway and certifierAddress above, and the servers running with the rebuilt WorldServer (world-snapshot-index.patch) and CacheServer (cache-client-addr.patch, with a Gateway "127.0.0.1" line in CacheServer.ini so the cache server takes the player's real address from the gateway). The converted game files must be in dist/assets (npm run convert). Leaving takes the world server a moment to save the character, so entering again straight after is turned away for a few seconds; the test waits up to 30 s for that. Run it once, not in a loop (the flood limit above counts its connections too).

The fight: the world test's last part but one is a fight on the real servers (to run only that part: npm run test:live:world -- -t fight). The first account's character checks that its bag was read (it looks for the starter food: lollipops and a biscuit), walks out of Flaris through the north gate and over the bridge to the field of Small Aibatts, picks the nearest one, and attacks it until it dies, for at most a minute. If the server says another player is already fighting that Aibatt, it picks another one, once. Then it checks that the server sent the character's EXP after the kill, and prints one line with the EXP the kill gave next to what the server's basic rule gives (2 at level 1, 1 at levels 2 and 3, none from level 4 on, as a Small Aibatt is weak). A different amount is not a failure: a server-wide EXP rate or an EXP event explains it. The test fails if the server says the attack speed is wrong, if a swing gets no damage back within 3 seconds, if no EXP message comes after the kill, or if any message from the server is misread. The food: a character the test made must carry exactly what a new character gets (3 lollipops and 1 biscuit); any other character must still carry at least one lollipop and one biscuit. The place: the character must stand where new characters start, beside Flaris's lodestar. An account with no character is fine: the test makes a new one and deletes it at the end. Afterwards, a character the test did not make walks back to where new characters start, beside the lodestar, but only if it is alive and still connected; one that died is sent back to life at the lodestar. If a run stops while that character is outside the town, the error says where it was left: before the next run, log in with it in the browser and walk it back through the north gate to the lodestar (the next fight also tries to walk it back first). Small Aibatts must be alive on the field just outside Flaris's north gate (one that dies comes back within half a minute), and no other player should be fighting them. The converted game files in dist/assets must be up to date (npm run convert).

The skill part: the world test's last part, with the same character (to run only that part: npm run test:live:world -- -t skill). If the character has a skill point left, it spends one on Clean Hit, as the skill window's + and Finish do, and checks that the server accepts it; with no point left (or Clean Hit already at its top level, 10) it spends nothing and says so in one line. Then it puts Clean Hit on the first bar's F4 slot (whatever was on F4 there is replaced), walks out to the Small Aibatts again, picks the nearest one, uses Clean Hit on it and checks that the server uses the skill and that the skill hits; its normal attacks then finish the Aibatt off, and it walks back to the lodestar, as after the fight (the same rules for a character left outside the town apply). Clean Hit can only be learned from level 3: a character below level 3 (or one that has not learned Clean Hit and has no skill point to learn it) is not a failure. This part is then skipped before the character moves, with one sentence saying why, and the rest of the test still runs.

Which character to use: the first account's first character should be a Vagrant of level 3 to 14 that stands beside Flaris's lodestar (where new characters start) and still carries some of its starter lollipops and biscuit (don't eat them all). Then both the fight and the skill part run. A brand-new character, or an account with no character (the test then makes one), runs the fight, and the skill part is skipped with its sentence until the character reaches level 3.
